Act as release orchestrator for this repository. The release takes finished private work to the
point where I make the public commit and the public push. The release workflow is the
authoritative procedure; it is injected into this session with the documentation workflow, the
documentation style guide, the workspace's publication slot and the two writer roles. Step 1 is the
export: `python AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/PUBLISHING/export.py`.

This session runs in the released plan's worktree, or in the integration worktree for a hotfix; the
merge into the integration branch happens in that branch's own worktree, as step 6 says. A hotfix
has no plan: there is no plan's `docs-pass.md` list and no plan to close. Your inputs are the
uncommitted public changes after a fresh export, the open plan's
`AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/PLANS/<plan>/docs-pass.md` list (delete each item once resolved) and this
conversation.

Your subagents are `ops-scout`, `document-writer`, `comment-writer`, and `phase-implementer` only
on my word. Any other subagent requires my explicit permission. Spawn every one in the background.
Ask me, as plain chat questions with a recommendation, about the documentation's sections and
titles, product defects and anything outside the workflow's own fixes. Never edit `AGENTS.md` or
`AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/` unless I say so, except deleting resolved `docs-pass.md` items and the plan
closure I approve.

I make the public commit and the public push myself unless I explicitly say otherwise; never commit
or push in the public repository without that word.

Finish by reporting what changed, what is deployed, the verification, and every open `docs-pass.md`
item with its reason. Then I check, commit and push.

=== gates.md ===
### Local environment

The project has no runtime configuration and no secrets. Cargo and its tools live in
`~/.cargo/bin`; when `cargo` is not on `PATH`, call `~/.cargo/bin/cargo`.

### Fast phase gate

For code changes, run named tests covering touched behavior and regressions, then:

```bash
cargo build
cargo test
cargo clippy -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --check
git diff --check
```

Documentation-only changes require changed-file reread plus `git diff --check`. Prose a change
writes or edits follows `AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/BUILDING/DOCUMENTATION-STYLE-GUIDE.md`. Tests follow
REPO-RULES §3a; the receipt states functions added/deleted.

### Experiment gate

This project has no experiments.

### Conditional gates

| Gate             | Run when                                                                 |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Rendered image   | The render loop, a material, the camera or the output format changed     |
| Agent generation | `AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/SUBAGENTS/**` or agent model assignment changed      |

Rendered-image gate: render a small image and check it opens and looks right.

```bash
cargo run --release -- --width 80 --height 40 --samples 4 --output /tmp/opencode/render.png
```

Until the command-line phase lands, `cargo run --release > /tmp/opencode/render.ppm` instead.

Agent-generation gate:

```bash
python -m json.tool AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/LOCAL/models.json >/dev/null
python AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/SUBAGENTS/gen_agents.py --check
```

"""Publishing data for one checkout, loaded by the workflow exporter.

Copy this file to ``AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/PUBLISHING/selection.py`` and replace the values with that
checkout's own selection. The lists below are an illustration, not a required layout.
``export.py`` beside it reads these names and nothing else; it carries no
paths of its own, so the same exporter publishes any checkout.

Source paths are relative to the checkout. Destinations are relative to ``TARGET_ROOT``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

# The public checkout this selection is mirrored into.
TARGET_ROOT: Path = Path.home() / "projects" / "public-checkout"

# Account homes that exist inside the served images, not on a host. Paths under them are not
# treated as a leaked host path.
CONTAINER_HOME_ACCOUNTS: tuple[bytes, ...] = ()

# Shared documentation authored here and published verbatim: every regular file under this root
# is mirrored to the same path, except the exclusions. Everything else is listed in FILE_MAP.
SHARED_DOCS_ROOT: str = "docs"
SHARED_DOCS_EXCLUDED: tuple[str, ...] = ("docs/private", "docs/USER-OWNED-TODO.md")

# (source, destination) for every exported file outside the shared documentation root. These two
# are an illustration; list the checkout's own.
FILE_MAP: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = (
    ("LICENSE", "LICENSE"),
    ("README.md", "README.md"),
)

# Explicit writes into a protected tree, checked exactly like FILE_MAP. Use these for deployment
# assets that live in the public checkout but are authored here.
PROTECTED_COPIES: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = ()

# Paths that exist only in the public checkout and must never be copied into or removed from it.
PUBLIC_ONLY: tuple[str, ...] = (".git", ".github", "config", ".env")

# Directory names the target cleanup may remove at any depth.
PRUNE_DIR_NAMES: frozenset[str] = frozenset({"__pycache__", "node_modules", ".cache"})

# Text that must never appear in an exported file: this checkout's private trees and tooling.
PRIVATE_MARKER_PATTERN: bytes = (
    rb"(?:docs/private|AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS|USER-OWNED-TODO|AGENTS\.md)"
)

# Exported shared Markdown may not link into these; private pages may not link into the subset in
# PRIVATE_DOC_LINK_FORBIDDEN. Private-to-private and private-to-shared links stay allowed.
SHARED_DOC_LINK_FORBIDDEN: tuple[str, ...] = (
    "docs/private",
    "docs/USER-OWNED-TODO.md",
    "AGENTS.md",
    "AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS",
)
PRIVATE_DOC_LINK_FORBIDDEN: tuple[str, ...] = (
    "docs/USER-OWNED-TODO.md",
    "AGENTS.md",
    "AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS",
)

# A leaked copy of these in the target stops the run before any mutation.
TARGET_GUARDED: tuple[str, ...] = (
    "docs/private",
    "docs/USER-OWNED-TODO.md",
    "AGENTS.md",
    "AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS",
)

385: def _without_code(text: str) -> str:
386:     """Return *text* with fenced code blocks and inline code spans blanked out."""
387:     kept: list[str] = []
388:     in_fence = False

398: def _link_destinations(text: str) -> list[str]:
399:     """Return destinations of real Markdown links, images and reference definitions in *text*.
400: 
401:     Fenced code blocks and inline code spans are ignored so examples are not read as links. A
402:     destination may sit on the line after its marker, so the code-free text is scanned as one
403:     buffer rather than per line.
404:     """
405:     body = _without_code(text)
406:     destinations = [match.group(1) or match.group(2) for match in _INLINE_LINK_RE.finditer(body)]
407:     destinations.extend(
408:         match.group(2) or match.group(3) for match in _REFERENCE_DEF_RE.finditer(body)

413: def _resolve_link(page_relative: PurePosixPath, destination: str) -> PurePosixPath | None:
414:     """Resolve one link destination to a normalized repository-relative path, or None.
415: 
416:     External links, bare fragments and repository-escaping paths return None; encoded segments
417:     and ``.``/``..`` steps are normalized before the guard lists are applied.
418:     """
419:     target = destination.strip()
420:     if not target or _ABSOLUTE_URL_RE.match(target):
421:         return None
422:     target = target.split("#", 1)[0].split("?", 1)[0]
423:     if not target:
424:         return None
425:     target = unquote(target).replace("\\", "/")
426:     if target.startswith("/"):
427:         resolved = PurePosixPath(target.lstrip("/"))
428:     else:
429:         resolved = page_relative.parent / target
430:     normalized = PurePosixPath(os.path.normpath(str(resolved)))
431:     if normalized.parts and normalized.parts[0] == "..":
432:         return None
433:     return normalized

=== docs/requirements.md ===
# Requirements

A small raytracer with no dependencies beyond the Rust standard library. It renders one fixed scene
and writes the image to a file. Every render is reproducible: the same options give the same bytes.

## Materials

1. Every object has a material. A ray that hits an object scatters by that material and the colour
   is the material's attenuation times the colour the scattered ray sees, up to a bounce limit of
   50; a ray that reaches the limit is black.
2. Diffuse material scatters in a random direction around the surface normal and attenuates by its
   albedo.
3. Metal material reflects about the normal, blurred by a fuzz factor in 0..=1, and attenuates by
   its albedo. A reflection that points into the surface is absorbed.
4. Glass material refracts by its refractive index using Snell's law, reflects on total internal
   reflection, and chooses reflection by Schlick's approximation otherwise. It does not attenuate.
5. Each pixel averages a configurable number of samples (default 16), jittered inside the pixel,
   with gamma 2 correction on output.
6. All randomness comes from the seeded generator in `src/rng.rs`, seeded with a fixed value.

## Geometry

7. Every hit records whether the ray hit the front face, and the normal always points against the
   ray.
8. Every hit records texture coordinates `(u, v)` in 0..=1: spheres by latitude and longitude,
   planes by the hit point's position along two axes in the plane, modulo 1, and triangles by their
   barycentric coordinates.
9. The scene can hold infinite planes (a point and a normal) and triangles (three vertices).
10. Every object reports an axis-aligned bounding box, and the scene list tests a ray against an
    object's box before the object. An infinite plane has no box and is always tested.

## Output and command line

11. The image is written as PNG, with no external crate: one IDAT chunk holding zlib data made of
    stored (uncompressed) deflate blocks, with correct CRC-32 and Adler-32 checksums. PPM stays
    available.
12. The command line takes `--width`, `--height`, `--samples`, `--output <path>` and
    `--format png|ppm`. The defaults are 400 by 200, 16 samples, `render.png` and the format from the
    output file's extension. An unknown option or a bad value prints a usage line and exits with a
    non-zero status.
13. While rendering, a progress line on standard error shows the share of rows done.

## Quality

14. `cargo build`, `cargo test`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` pass.

# Shared design: plan-a-A1 + plan-b-B1 (`HitRecord`)

Settled between the plan-a and plan-b orchestrators. Both plans reach this design on their own
branches; commits never move between branches, no branch is merged into another, and the release
merges both into the integration branch and resolves the textual conflicts in `src/hittable.rs` and
`src/sphere.rs` by the shape below.

## Target merged record

```rust
pub struct HitRecord {
    pub t: f64,
    pub point: Vec3,
    pub normal: Vec3,      // always faces against the ray
    pub front_face: bool,  // true when the ray hit the outside
    pub u: f64,
    pub v: f64,
    pub material: Rc<dyn Material>,
}
```

Derives `Clone` only. `Copy` is gone with the `Rc` field, and `Debug` is dropped because
`Rc<dyn Material>` is not `Debug` and nothing prints a hit record. The `Material` trait gains no
`Debug` supertrait.

`normal` always faces against the ray (`docs/requirements.md` item 7). `front_face` is true when the
ray hit the outside of the surface; that flag, not the normal's direction, tells entering from
leaving.

## One construction path

```rust
HitRecord::new(ray, t, point, outward_normal, u, v, material)
```

- `front_face = ray.direction.dot(outward_normal) < 0.0`;
- `normal = if front_face { outward_normal } else { -outward_normal }`;
- records every field.

No record literal and no second face-side helper survives the merge on either branch. That rule
covers A1's `src/material.rs` tests too: the merge routes their records through
`HitRecord::new(...)` with the outward normal and `u`, `v`.

## Merged `Sphere::hit` tail

```rust
let point = ray.at(t);
let outward_normal = (point - self.center) / self.radius;
let theta = (-outward_normal.y).acos();
let phi = (-outward_normal.z).atan2(outward_normal.x) + PI;
Some(HitRecord::new(
    ray,
    t,
    point,
    outward_normal,
    phi / (2.0 * PI),
    theta / PI,
    Rc::clone(&self.material),
))
```

## What each plan does on its own branch

- **plan-b / B1:** the record gains `front_face`, `u`, `v` and keeps its current derives; the
  constructor takes six arguments, without a material; `Sphere::hit` fills `u` and `v` from the
  outward normal's latitude and longitude, so a back-face hit of the same point gets the same texture
  coordinates. No material exists on this branch. Later plan-b shapes (B2/B3) use the same
  constructor without a material and take the object's material as the final argument once the
  material seam is merged in.
- **plan-a / A1:** unchanged as detailed. The record keeps its material field and literal
  construction on this branch. The merge combines the two: the record gains `front_face`, `u`, `v`
  and loses `Copy` and `Debug`, and `Sphere::hit` becomes the merged tail above.

## What A2 may rely on after the merge

- `hit.normal` always faces the ray; `hit.front_face` is true on entry, false when leaving.
- Glass decides entering versus leaving from `hit.front_face` and works with `hit.normal` in the
  glass frame: `cos_theta = -ray_in.direction.unit().dot(hit.normal)`, positive on entry. No outward
  normal and no second face flag.
- A1's `Lambertian` and `Metal` formulas stay as written; both already use a normal that faces the
  incoming ray. Their comments say "the normal facing the ray" after the merge, not "outward
  normal".

## A2 on plan-a's branch before the merge

Glass derives the face side locally from the outward normal A1 leaves on the record
(`front_face = ray_in.direction.dot(hit.normal) < 0.0`, normal flipped from it), uses
`cos_theta = -ray_in.direction.unit().dot(normal)`, and **the release replaces those two lines with
`hit.front_face` and the facing `hit.normal` as part of the merge itself**, not as optional cleanup.
That local derivation is temporary branch code, never part of the merged shape.

## Materials for the new shapes at the merge

Requirement 1 says every object has a material, but plan-b's branch has no material seam when B2 and
B3 add planes and triangles. The release gives each new shape a material field and passes
`Rc::clone(&self.material)` as the constructor's last argument, and names a scene material for it.

At the merge the ground plane and the triangle are both matte: the ground takes the mid-grey the
current ground sphere uses, and the triangle a distinct dull green so it reads clearly.

# Shared design: plan-a-A1 + plan-c-C3 (`render` loop, generator, gamma, progress line)

Settled between the plan-a and plan-c orchestrators. Both plans reach this design on their own
branches; commits never move between branches, no branch is merged into another, and the release
merges both into the integration branch and resolves the textual conflicts in `src/main.rs` by the
shape below. plan-c leads this pair; plan-c's C1 is already landed, so the merged `render` starts
from plan-c's code and A1's material loop lands inside it.

## Target merged `render`

```rust
fn render(width: usize, height: usize, samples: usize) -> Vec<Colour> {
    let world = scene();
    let camera = Camera::new(width as f64 / height as f64);
    let mut rng = Rng::new(SEED);
    let mut pixels = Vec::with_capacity(width * height);
    for row in (0..height).rev() {
        for column in 0..width {
            let mut colour = Colour::new(0.0, 0.0, 0.0);
            for _ in 0..samples {
                let u = column as f64 / (width - 1) as f64; // A3 draws the jitter here
                let v = row as f64 / (height - 1) as f64;
                colour = colour + ray_colour(&camera.ray(u, v), &world, &mut rng);
            }
            pixels.push(colour / samples as f64);
        }
        eprint!("\r{} of {} rows", height - row, height);
    }
    eprintln!();
    pixels
}
```

## Rules the merge follows

1. `render(width, height, samples) -> Vec<Colour>` is frozen by plan-c's C1. On plan-a's branch A1
   still builds `render(width, height)` with the `WIDTH` and `HEIGHT` constants, because that is the
   branch's API at its base; that is not a conflict, it is branch state. The merged tree takes C1's
   signature and its settings/command-line path, and A1's material loop lands inside `ray_colour`.
   `WIDTH` and `HEIGHT` do not survive the merge.
2. Nesting is row, then column, then sample, then bounce: one trace per sample, with the same
   generator threaded through every bounce of that trace.
3. Exactly one `Rng::new(SEED)` is created at the top of `render` and passed `&mut` down into
   `ray_colour`. No second generator, no global, no per-pixel or per-sample reseeding. Consumption
   order is row-major, so a fixed sample count reproduces byte-identically.
4. `ray_colour` keeps its name and its 50-bounce material loop, returns linear radiance, returns
   black at the bounce limit and the sky gradient on a miss.
5. Averaging happens in linear space in `render`. `to_byte` applies gamma 2 (`sqrt`) once to the
   averaged channel and stays the single output conversion that both the PNG and PPM writers use.
   Gamma is never applied per sample.
6. `render` returns the pixel vector unchanged to `run(&Settings)`, which encodes and writes it as
   C1 leaves it. Neither writer changes in this settlement.
7. The progress line is the two `eprint`/`eprintln` calls inside the row loop after the column loop,
   inside `render`. It counts rows only and is independent of samples and bounces. Neither A1 nor A3
   moves, renames or re-implements it.
8. A3 keeps this signature and the command-line-owned defaults (400 by 200, 16 samples). Its only
   change is replacing the fixed `u`, `v` with jittered ones drawn from the same generator.

## Sample count guarantees

- `samples` is always at least 1 by the time `render` runs: C1's option parser rejects a value below
  1 with the usage line and exit status 2, and `tests/cli.rs` already covers `--samples 0`. Nothing
  in `render`, A1 or A3 may add a second guard for it.
- Once materials consume the generator, the image legitimately depends on the sample count; that is
  requirement 5. C1's recorded "same bytes at every sample count" described the pre-randomness state
  and is not preserved, and no test asserts that invariance (`tests/cli.rs` uses the option only as a
  value and as a rejected bad value), so nothing is deleted for it. What must hold afterwards: each
  fixed sample count reproduces byte-identically across runs.

## A3 draw order

For each sample, before the bounce trace: two `next_f64` draws offset `u` and `v` inside the pixel,
then the bounce scattering draws for that trace. Row-major across the image. Two draws per sample is
the fixed order, so A3's detail and the merge cannot disagree about where the draws happen.

# Output Plan

> **Status:** scoped forward plan, revised 2026-11-24 on branch `plan-c`.
> **Scope:** how the program is run and what it writes: the PNG writer, the command line and the
> progress line (`docs/requirements.md` items 11 to 13).
> **Out of scope:** materials, sampling, jitter and scattering (the materials plan); shapes, hit
> data and bounding boxes (the geometry plan).
> **Target:** a correct, small hobby raytracer. Every phase here is product work; no phase is an
> experiment.
>
> **How to use this plan:** expand exactly one phase into an implementation-grade phase from
> current code before coding. Discuss and edit phase boundaries here first.

## Phase status

| Phase | Title | Status | Gate level | Depends on | Phase file | Exit state | Move-on gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | PNG writer and command line | done | standard | - | `done/C1-png-writer-and-command-line.md` | the program writes a real PNG at the chosen size, path and format from the command line | fast gate green, the written PNG opens, PPM still writes |
| C2 | (merged into C1) | not applicable | - | - | - | - | - |
| C3r | Shared render settlement | done | minimal | C1 | `done/C3r-shared-render-settlement.md` | the merged render shape is recorded for this branch and the merge | plan documents re-read, `git diff --check` clean, no product code moved |
| C3 | Progress line | done | standard | C1 | `done/C3-progress-line.md` | rendering shows the share of rows done on standard error | fast gate green, progress observed, image unchanged |
| Z1 | Closing survey and user acceptance | done | minimal | C1 + C3 | `done/Z1-closing-survey-and-user-acceptance.md` | the closing survey note is written and the user accepts the result | the user accepts |

Every phase is done or not applicable. The plan's work is complete and awaits the release, which
closes it.

C2 was folded into C1 so that PPM never becomes unreachable code and the format choice exists in
the same change that makes `render.png` the default.

## How to implement this plan

1. Read `docs/requirements.md` items 11 to 13, the README, `AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/LOCAL/gates.md` and
   the code the selected phase touches before detailing it.
2. Never invent a name, signature, path or option. If something the phase names does not exist,
   stop and report drift.
3. One phase at a time. Commits whenever useful, no squashing, never on `main`.
4. Product code: no dependency, no hardcoded second path, no `allow(dead_code)` to paper over
   plumbing. `Cargo.toml` stays dependency-free.
5. Run the fast gate in `AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/LOCAL/gates.md`, plus the rendered-image conditional
   gate whenever the render loop or the output format changes.
6. Fail loudly: a bad option, a bad value or an unwritable output path reports and exits non-zero;
   no silent fallback format or path.
7. Update the README in the phase that makes its usage line wrong. A genuine deferral to the release
   goes in `docs-pass.md`.

## Binding design rules

1. No dependency. The PNG is built from stored (uncompressed) deflate blocks, with CRC-32 per chunk
   and Adler-32 in the zlib trailer computed in the writer itself. No crate, no build script, no
   bundled compressor.
2. The PNG writer lives in `src/png.rs`. The PPM writer stays `write_ppm` in `src/main.rs`. `main`
   resolves the options and calls exactly one of them; there is no third output path.
3. Options resolve once into one set of settings before rendering. Defaults are 400 by 200, 16
   samples, `render.png`, and the format from the output file's extension. An explicit `--format`
   wins over the extension. An unknown option, a value that does not parse, an unrecognised format
   or an unrecognised output extension prints a usage line and exits non-zero.
4. `--samples` is accepted and validated here and passed into the render loop as a parameter; each
   pixel averages that many rays. The rays are not jittered yet, because scattering belongs to the
   materials plan, so today every sample count produces the same bytes at `samples` times the cost.
   That is the honest intermediate state: this plan must not add jitter or scattering, and the
   materials plan fills it in. The render signature is the seam the materials plan consumes.
5. Standard output stays clean: the image goes only to the output file and the progress line only to
   standard error. No image bytes on stdout.
6. Rendering stays reproducible: the same options give the same bytes. No new randomness, no time,
   no environment-dependent output.
7. Single-threaded, no `unsafe`, one concept per module, shared types in the module that defines the
   concept. Every module starts with a `//!` line.
8. Docs follow the change: the README run example is updated by the phase that makes it wrong. The
   rendered-image fallback sentence in `AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/LOCAL/gates.md` stays until the release,
   because that file is shared by every worktree and the sentence is still true where this plan's
   command line has not landed; its removal is recorded in `docs-pass.md`.

## Starting state

- `src/main.rs` renders a fixed 200 by 100 through `render(width, height)` and writes ASCII PPM
  (P3, maximum 255) to standard output through `write_ppm(out, width, height, pixels)`; `to_byte`
  clamps and scales a channel. There is no option parsing and `std::env::args` is unused.
- Two tests in `src/main.rs` pin the centre pixel and the top row from `render(200, 100)`.
- `README.md` shows `cargo run > image.ppm`. `AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/LOCAL/gates.md` carries the same
  fallback ("until the command-line phase lands, `cargo run --release > render.ppm`").
- There is no `src/png.rs` and `Cargo.toml` has no dependency.
- Known gaps: no PNG writer, no command line, no progress line, and the rendered size is 200 by 100
  rather than the required 400 by 200.

What later phases inherit:

- `render` gains the sample count; `write_ppm` stays reachable through `--format ppm`.
- The output file is the only place the image goes; stdout carries nothing but what the user asks
  for.
- One resolved settings value per render; later phases add behaviour behind it, not a second parse.

## Scoped phases

### C3r - Shared render settlement

Records the `render` design settled with the materials plan in
`PLANS/shared/plan-a-A1+plan-c-C3.md`: the merged signature and nesting, one seeded `Rng` at the top
of `render`, linear averaging with the single gamma 2 in `to_byte`, the two progress calls inside the
row loop, A3's jitter draw order, the command-line `samples >= 1` guarantee and the fact that no test
asserts sample-count invariance. No product code changes on this branch; C3's progress line already
matches the settlement and keeps its existing detail.

### C1 - PNG writer and command line

**Status:** done.
**Depends on:** none (the first phase).
**Scope:** the program stops writing PPM to standard output and instead resolves a small set of
command-line options and writes the image to a file as PNG or PPM. This is the phase that makes the
output side of the product match requirements 11 and 12.
**Expected gate level:** standard.

**Starting state / reason:**
- The image only exists as PPM on stdout; there is no file, no size choice and no PNG.
- Requirement 11 wants a dependency-free PNG, requirement 12 the five options and their defaults.
- PPM must stay available, which is exactly why the format choice lands together with the PNG
  writer: switching the default to `render.png` on its own would leave `write_ppm` uncalled.

**Likely areas to touch:**
- `src/png.rs` - new module with the writer.
- `src/main.rs` - option parsing, the resolved settings, the render signature, `main`.
- `README.md` - the run example.

**Must not:**
- Add a dependency, a build script or any real deflate compression.
- Delete `write_ppm` or bypass it with a second PPM path.

**Verification shape:**

**Exit:** `cargo run` writes `render.png`; size, sample count, output path and format are honoured;
PPM still writes through `--format ppm`; a bad option prints usage and exits non-zero.
**Move-on gate:** fast gate green, the written PNG opens and looks right, PPM still writes,
work committed.

### C3 - Progress line

**Status:** done.
**Depends on:** C1 (it consumes the render loop and the resolved settings C1 leaves).
**Scope:** while rendering, the program reports the share of rows done on standard error, updating
one line instead of printing a new one per row.
**Expected gate level:** standard.

**Starting state / reason:**
- Rendering is silent; at 400 by 200 with 16 samples it takes long enough that silence looks like a
  hang.

**Likely areas to touch:**
- `src/main.rs` - the render loop and its caller.

**TODOs:**
1. Report the row share on standard error as rows finish, overwriting one line.
2. Leave the finished line terminated so later output is not glued onto it.
3. Keep the image bytes exactly what they were for the same options.

**Must not:**
- Write progress to standard output or into the image file.
- Add a timing, throttling or verbosity option; the requirements ask for one line.
- Test the exact progress text or its refresh cadence.
- Change pixels, sampling or the scene.

**Verification shape:**
- Fast gate.
- Rendered-image gate (this phase owns it): a small render with the progress line observed on
  standard error, and the same image bytes as before the change for identical options.
- No separate acceptance test beyond the agent-run checks.

**Exit:** a render shows its row share on standard error while it runs.
**Move-on gate:** fast gate green, progress observed, image unchanged, work committed.

### Z1 - Closing survey and user acceptance

**Status:** done.
**Depends on:** C1 + C3.
**Scope:** the binding closing survey of everything this plan added or changed, then the user's
acceptance of the result. The orchestrator executes it: it dispatches the scouts, writes the note and
runs the acceptance render.
**Expected gate level:** minimal.

**Starting state / reason:**

**Likely areas to touch:**

- Nothing else; findings are reported, not fixed.

   the docs this plan touched. Each reads whatever context outside its area it needs, and reports an
   out-of-scope problem with the evidence it already has instead of investigating it.
2. Dispatch ONE independent read-only `ops-scout` to cross-check every saved finding, claim by claim,
   with evidence. Areas get no per-area checker.
3. The orchestrator writes the dated note in `benchmarks/` from the saved returns and the
   cross-check. Every finding cites `path:line` from the current tree.
4. The orchestrator renders the scene through the real command line, compares it with requirements
   11 to 13, and presents the note, the findings and the render to the user.

**Must not:**
- Fix anything inside this phase; findings go to the user.
- Delegate the note to a phase implementer or a reviewer, skip the cross-check, merge areas into one
  read, or write the note from memory.
- Tell a scout to report only on the diff.
- Change product code, docs, the phase files or the plan's status rows.

**Verification shape:**
- The four scout returns and the cross-check return exist; the note, written by the orchestrator,

- The acceptance render is produced through the real command line.

**Exit:** the dated survey note is written and the user has accepted the result.
**Move-on gate:** the user accepts the survey and the result; the plan is then ready for the
release, which closes it.

# PLANS

Working plans live here. A plan is a **folder**, not a single file.

## Folder convention

```
PLANS/shared/<pair>.md  # an overlap design two parallel plans agreed on, one copy for both
PLANS/<slug>/         # <slug> is the plan's branch and worktree name; never `shared` or `archive`
  full-plan.md        # scope, design rules, and the phase status table (single source of truth)
  scope.md            # the plan's work fence, injected into every agent working on the plan
  handoff.md          # the plan orchestrator's living handoff; children never read it
  autonomous-decisions.md  # orchestrator-only working record, created when a decision needs recording
  docs-pass.md        # items explicitly deferred to the release, kept until the release clears them
  phases/<id>.md      # one detailed, implementation-grade phase — created only when that phase is active
  done/<id>.md        # a completed phase compressed to its frozen contract
  benchmarks/<name>-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md  # dated experiment/result/run notes (immutable records)
```

- `/plan-new` creates the plan folder with its starting `full-plan.md`, `scope.md` and
  `handoff.md`, together with the plan's branch and worktree.
- Author `full-plan.md` first (see `../PLANNING/PLAN-AUTHORING-SCOPING.md`). Phases stay
  scoped/vague there; the status table marks one phase `active` at a time.
- Plan and phase files hold current state only; superseded text is replaced, not annotated with history.
- Expand the active phase into one `phases/<id>.md` file just before building it (see
  `../PLANNING/PLAN-PHASE-DETAILING.md`). In serial orchestration, `phase-advancer` owns
  this work, including initial phase detail. The file carries exact steps, tests, and a
  `User test` acceptance section the agent runs unless it names capability only user has.
- An implementer loads `full-plan.md` (top matter + design rules + status table) plus the
  one active phase file — never a monolith. That bound is what stops a weak model from
  forgetting and hallucinating.
- On completion, compress `phases/<id>.md` into `done/<id>.md` (frozen contract only) and
  flip the status table row to `done`.
- If a phase lands but fails its retest, re-detail the same `phases/<id>.md` in place per
  `../PLANNING/PLAN-PHASE-REMEDIATION.md` (keep working parts, fix steps at full grade); the row
  stays `active` until the retest passes.

- Dated experiment results, benchmark/run records and acceptance-run notes go in
  `benchmarks/`, never the plan root or `phases/`. They are frozen evidence: cite them from
  `full-plan.md` as `benchmarks/<note>.md` and from `done/` as `../benchmarks/<note>.md`.
  Plan-scope working documents that are not run records (for example a scope/review note
  for a split phase) stay at the plan root.

- Every plan runs the same lifecycle: detail and implement phases until every phase, the closing
  survey included, is done; then the release (`../BUILDING/RELEASE-WORKFLOW.md`, the `/release` command), which ends with
  closure.
- Phases update every page their change touches and may create new pages; splitting existing pages
  belongs to the release. `docs-pass.md` lists only the items explicitly deferred to the release
  instead, each with its file or page and what is wrong. The
  orchestrator creates it at the first deferral and adds each one as soon as a phase document, a
  child report or the user makes it. Items are never parked only
  in a `done/` contract, a phase file or the chat. The release reads it as input and
  deletes each item it resolves; the plan closes only with the list empty or every remaining item
  accepted by the user.
- `autonomous-decisions.md` is created in the active plan's root only when the orchestrator needs
  to record a decision. It holds each autonomous decision, its reason and how to undo it. It is
  orchestrator-only context, never read or edited by children or copied into their briefs.

Execution rules: `../BUILDING/WORKING-FROM-PLANS.md`.

## Archive

A plan whose every phase is `done` or `not applicable`, with no open milestone, the user's acceptance
of its closing survey results (`../PLANNING/PLAN-AUTHORING-SCOPING.md` §3b), a finished release
(`../BUILDING/RELEASE-WORKFLOW.md`) with its `docs-pass.md` list cleared or accepted, and explicit user
authorization to close it, is complete. Its folder is moved unchanged with
a plain `mv` to `PLANS/archive/<slug>/` (the advancer that flips its last row does this; the workflow plugin commits the workspace root), and only the path
pointers the move breaks are repointed, inside the moved plan and wherever else they appear. Archived plans are frozen: they are
never edited and never loaded in a work session; read one only when the current phase explicitly names an old contract in it
(`PLANS/archive/<slug>/done/<id>.md`). Plans that are active or have an open milestone stay at `PLANS/<slug>/`.

Archived text records the contract at completion, not the current implementation; consult current
source and permanent docs for current truth. Archived files carry their actual archive date. Archive
